newsitem.title: BELGIUM: De Silguy "encouraged" by French audit response.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy "encouraged" by French audit response.

text.p: The European Union's Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault De Silguy said on Monday the French government's response to the public-finance audit had been "encouraging".

In a statement released after France's socialist government raised taxes on big business to bring down this year's public deficit De Silguy said the budget clean up measures went in the right direction.
"The response of the French government to the results of the public finance audit is encouraging," he said in a statement. "The budget clean-up measures announced go in the right direction."

De Silguy, the Commissioner responsible for seeing through the EU's plans for economic and monetary union, said that the hardest had been done in France's efforts to reduce the budget deficit, which had fallen to 4.2 percent in 1996 from 5.6 percent in 1993.
"What remains to be done is fine-tuning," he said in the statement. "They should not slow down efforts now that we are on the home strait."
The audit found France's public deficit to be running well above the level required to qualify for a single European currency.

The audit, ordered by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on taking office last month showed the 1997 deficit was running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, significantly beyond the three percent limit set by the Maastricht Treaty.

De Silguy, while avoiding commenting directly on what the audit and government response meant for France's ambition to be in the first countries to join the single currency, said France's vocation was "to remain one of the motors of European construction."
